concepts.def: X̄ = (1/n) Σ X_i for a sample of size n.
If X has mean μ, variance σ², then X̄ has mean μ and variance σ²/n.
For large n, X̄ is approximately N(μ, σ²/n) regardless of X's distribution.
σ/√n is the standard deviation of X̄.

mcqs.q: What does a larger standard deviation tell you about a data set?
options: The mean of the data set is larger.
The data values are more spread out around the mean.
The mode is most affected because the outlier becomes the new most common value.
There are more data points in the set.

mcqs.q: What is the derivative of a constant, like d/dx(5)?
options: There are more data points in the set.
0 — constants do not change with x.
The derivative of 5 is 1 because all constants differentiate to 1.
The derivative of 5 is 5 because the constant stays the same.

mcqs.q: If a data set has an extreme outlier, which average is most affected?
options: The median is most affected because the outlier shifts the middle.
The mode is most affected because the outlier becomes the new most common value.
There are more data points in the set.
The mean — because every value (including the outlier) contributes to it.
